claims.statement: Quest types and instances are split: an instance stores only its type name plus the current step index, so editing a template's steps never rewrites existing instance data (I1).

KV stores scalars only, so every logical table field is flattened into named scalar keys with newline-joined name lists — the same shape entity uses, and the reason a `nil` `on_enter` lands as an empty string.

Advancement is monotonic (`advance` only +1) and terminal states are one-way: any primitive after `done`/`abandoned` raises `YGG-PKG-QUEST-TERMINAL`, while an explicit `jump` leaves a `quest.jumped` record so history stays auditable.

The derived event surface is fixed at four names plus `quest.jumped`; they ride `ygg.emit`'s internal derived-event channel and are not kernel events, so a package can never expand the kernel event face.
The 24-case count (20 behaviour + 4 perf) is pinned by the package's own fixture, and the event assertion is set equality rather than containment, which is what makes I6 testable.
The smoke file is a file-level assertion that keeps the package loadable from the consuming fixture even when `--filter` targets mod-side files; it carries no counted cases.
`ygg.kv.set` accepts only four scalar kinds through `value_from_lua` (a table write fails with `unsupported payload type: table`), which is the host-side fact the flat-key layout is derived from.
The package declares its own dependencies and requires only codec's key-naming surface plus a host handle, so `quest.keys` can be handed to `codec.export` without the package owning serialization.
